title: World tuning
description: Gameplay tuning owned by the World domain (Battleground Bible; ADR-011 §12, §17): the battleground's grey-box layout, which the map commandlet bakes and the server spawns from, and its structures. Distances are in world units; X runs up the screen and Y to its right. VeyraWorld binds it to FVeyraWorldTuning.

terrain.description: The battleground's ground levels and the runs between them (ADR-040 §3), in world units: they decide its slopes, so how it is walked.

islandZ.description: Each Flux Well's island platform, above the water.

laneShoulder.description: How far beside a road the ground stays at the road's level; the masses keep clear of it (ADR-073 §2).

jungleRise.description: The run over which ground climbs from a road, a keep or a clearing to the jungle.

bankWidth.description: The run from the water's edge to the top of its bank.

underwaterShelfShare.description: Under the water, the share of a bank's run over which the bed rises to the waterline: the shore's shelf.

clearingCoreShare.description: The share of a clearing's radius that stays level.

clearingFadeShare.description: The share of a clearing's radius beyond its level core over which the ground returns to the jungle.

boundaryZ.description: The rim's height at the floor's edge.

boundaryWidth.description: The rim's band inside the floor's edge: the playable square is the floor less this each side (ADR-073 §2, §3).

wallFootingClearance.description: How far a terrain box's collision reaches below the lowest ground under it.

riverPoint.description: A river channel's control: where its centreline passes and how wide its water is there, in world units.

river.description: The river both teams share (ADR-040 §6; author ruling 2026-10-05): Team A's half authored, Team B's its rotation half a turn about the centre. The main channel runs from the centre (its first control is 0, 0) outward off the floor; each island's side channel leaves and rejoins it around a Flux Well site.

samplesPerSegment.description: Samples to each span between controls.

walkableEnd.description: How far along the main channel from the centre its water is ground (ADR-073 §1): beyond it, both ways, the river drops through a gorge of falls that rock masses close off.

bedZ.description: The riverbed units wade on, below the surface.

flowSpeed.description: How fast the water is drawn flowing, in units a second. Presentation only.

site.description: The Flux Well site (an index into fluxWells.sites) the island carries.

point.description: A point on the floor, in world units.

lane.description: One Fluxway (Battleground Bible §2, §4) and Team A's structures on it; Team B's are their mirror.

points.description: The lane's path from Team A's base to Team B's. Turned half a turn about the centre and reversed, it must be one of the lanes: top onto bot, mid onto itself.

width.description: How wide the lane's road is drawn.

inhibitorDistance.description: Team A's inhibitor: its distance along the lane from Team A's end.

spireDistances.description: Team A's three Spires (Battleground Bible §10): their distances beyond the inhibitor, strictly rising, so the last is the outer Spire.

spireSides.description: Which side of the road each Spire stands, in spireDistances' order (author ruling 2026-10-12): +1 the lane's left seen walking from Team A's end in world x/y, -1 its right. Each stands layout.spireOffset from the centre line.

fluxbornSpawnDistance.description: Where Team A's Fluxborn of this lane spawn: their distance along the lane from Team A's end, clear of the inhibitor (Battleground Bible §17).

structure.description: One kind of structure's stats and body. Structures have their own Armor and Magic Resist (Combat Bible §33).

capsuleRadius.description: The body's radius: what attacks reach and what blocks movement.

stats.description: Base stats (FVeyraStatBlock), as a Vanguard's: Max Health, Move Speed and Attack Speed above 0, the rest at least 0.

homingProjectile.description: A homing projectile, which terrain does not stop (ADR-008 §9).

shape.description: A hit shape (ADR-009 §4). Each kind uses its own sizes; the others are 0.

basicAttack.description: A basic attack, with the profile Vanguards use (Combat Bible §4, §48; ADR-008 §2).

range.description: Edge to edge, in units (Combat Bible §40).

windupFraction.description: The part of each attack's interval before Commit; the rest is backswing.

acquisitionRadius.description: How far past its edge the unit looks for an enemy.

minimumIntervalSeconds.description: The shortest time between attacks whatever the Attack Speed; 0 for none.

projectile.description: A ranged attack's homing projectile; empty for melee.

cleave.description: Where the attack cleaves when something makes it cleave.

waveUnits.description: Some Fluxborn of one kind, by its ID in fluxborn.units.

wildlifeSpecies.description: One species of jungle wildlife (Battleground Bible §8; ADR-014 §2). Camps never evolve (§17).

traits.description: The trait its camp's clear grants the Vanguard credited with the last kill: at most one status in Abilities.json, or none.

camp.description: One of Team A's camps; Team B's is its mirror (Battleground Bible §7, §17).

id.description: The camp's own name (ADR-073 §1): its ground is the layout clearing of the same id. Two camps may share a species, never an id.

count.description: How many creatures of its species it holds.

center.description: Where it sits: its leash's centre.

spawnSeconds.description: When it first spawns, in match-clock seconds (§17: two spawn groups, 0:55 and 1:07).

respawnSeconds.description: How long after its last creature dies it spawns again (§17: each camp on its own timer).

leashRadius.description: How far from its centre its creatures fight before they walk home and heal (§17).

spacing.description: With several creatures, how far from the centre each stands.

keep.description: Team A's walled keep (ADR-073 §1): its floor, its wall runs, and the gates that break them. Team B's is its rotation.

floor.description: The keep's floor: a simple polygon, its corners in order.

walls.description: The keep's wall runs: architecture along the floor's edge, broken only where a gate stands.

gates.description: One gate to each lane, where its lane leaves the keep.

clearing.description: One of Team A's clearings (ADR-073 §1): open ground kept at its full size. A camp's ground is the clearing of its id; a glade is a junction, river mouth, pocket or ford.

route.description: One of Team A's jungle routes (ADR-073 §1): open ground along a path, as wide as its width. Team B's is its rotation.

width.description: The route's full width: rotation 1000, approach 700, outer 900 (provisional).

massRules.description: How the rock and forest masses are derived and turned into terrain (ADR-073 §2, §3, §5).

minThickness.description: No mass thinner than this survives: thinner leftovers become open ground.

minArea.description: Leftovers smaller than this, in square units, become open ground.

simplifyTolerance.description: How far a mass's outline may move when simplified.

riverMargin.description: Walkable bank beside the water, each side.

forestMinArea.description: Inner masses at least this large are forest; smaller ones rock; masses touching the floor's rim are cliff.

edgeThickness.description: How deep each terrain box along a mass's edge reaches inside it.

edgeMaxLength.description: The longest a single edge box may be: longer edges are split.

cornerRadius.description: Each convex corner of a mass is rounded to this radius, and spikes narrower than twice it cut back, so no corner is sharper than a right angle and its edge boxes stay inside it.

visualTolerance.description: How far a mass mesh's footprint may lie from its gameplay edge.

masses.description: GENERATED by Game/Scripts/Crucible/BuildCrucibleMasses.py, never edited by hand (ADR-073 §2): the rock and forest masses of both teams, and the hash of the inputs they were derived from.

points.description: Its outline, counter-clockwise in world x/y.

fluxbornDefinition.description: One kind of Fluxborn (Battleground Bible §4; ADR-011 §7).

role.description: Frontline (Striders), Ranged (Sparks) or Siege (Breakers, which put structures in range first, §19).

schemaVersion.description: Version of this file's format. A build reads exactly one version.

layout.description: The grey-box battleground (Battleground Bible §2, macro shape ruled 2026-09-28): bases in opposite corners, top and bot lanes along the sides set in from the edge with outer jungle beyond, mid on the diagonal, the river curving across the other. Team A's half is authored; Team B's is its rotation half a turn about the centre (author ruling 2026-10-05).

halfExtent.description: The square floor reaches this far from the centre in each direction.

surface.description: World-owned ground search bounds and maximum walkable placement slope; provisional production terrain envelope.

lanes.description: Top, Mid and Bottom, once each.

denseFog.description: Team A's Dense Fog, the battleground's bush (Battleground Bible §11; Vision Bible §2; ADR-016 §4): circles wholly in Team A's half, at the spots ADR-016 §11 lists. Team B's is their mirror; circles that touch are one fog volume.

spireOffset.description: How far each Spire stands from its lane's centre line, on the side spireSides gives (author ruling 2026-10-12): beside the road, not on it.

clearings.description: Team A's clearings: camps' ground and glades; Team B's are their rotation.

routes.description: Team A's jungle routes; Team B's are their rotation.

wallHalfHeight.description: Half the height of the terrain raised along masses and keep walls: taller than any body it blocks.

fountain.description: Where the team's Vanguards start and respawn.

fountainRadius.description: How far from the fountain point a Vanguard counts as at its fountain (§12).

structures.description: Every kind of structure's stats and body (Battleground Bible §5, §10, §18). Canon gives no numbers.

inhibitor.description: An inhibitor reconstructs after it falls (Battleground Bible §10, §18).

rebuildSeconds.description: How long after its destruction an inhibitor reconstructs at full Health, in seconds (§10: 3 minutes).

primeWell.description: The passive Prime Well regenerates missing Health while all its team's inhibitors stand (Battleground Bible §18).

regenerationFractionPerSecond.description: Missing Health restored per second, as a fraction of its Max Health.

towerAttack.description: A lane Spire's or base-defense tower's shot (Combat Bible §33, §55): Physical, not a basic attack, never a crit.

damage.description: Each shot's base damage, before the consecutive-hit ramp.

range.description: Attack range, edge to edge (Combat Bible §40).

projectileSpeed.description: The homing shot's speed, in units per second.

projectileRadius.description: The shot's own radius; it lands when it touches the target's body.

thinkSeconds.description: How often a tower reconsiders its target, in seconds: how soon it answers aggression or a target leaving.

towerRamp.description: Consecutive tower shots against the same Vanguard escalate, and reset on target loss or switch (Combat Bible §33).

perShot.description: Damage added per consecutive shot, as a fraction of the base; 0.2 is +20%.

maxStacks.description: The most ramp stacks a shot can carry.

backdoor.description: Backdoor protection (Battleground Bible §19; Combat Bible §33): with no attacking Fluxborn near, a lane Spire, base tower or Prime Well takes less damage, climbing to a maximum; an attacking Fluxborn arriving removes it at once. It never lifts invulnerability.

radius.description: How near the structure's centre an attacking Fluxborn lifts the protection.

maxReduction.description: The most damage it removes, from 0 to below 1.

rampSeconds.description: Seconds from none to the maximum.

updateSeconds.description: How often it is brought up to date.

fluxborn.description: The lane Fluxborn (Battleground Bible §4, §17, §19; ADR-011 §7). Team Flux strengthens them; nothing else scales them over time.

units.description: Every kind of Fluxborn, keyed by its stable ID.

ai.description: How every Fluxborn's server controller behaves.

thinkSeconds.description: How often it reconsiders its target and path, in seconds of world time.

aggressionResponseRange.description: How far past its edge an enemy Vanguard hurting a nearby ally draws it (§19).

leashRange.description: How far from its lane's path it engages a target, and strays itself: a target farther out is let go, and so is any target once the Fluxborn itself is farther out; then it returns (ADR-065 §2).

waypointAcceptance.description: How close to a waypoint counts as reaching it.

corpseSeconds.description: How long a fallen Fluxborn's body stays before it is removed.

avoidanceConsiderationRadius.description: How far each Fluxborn looks for others to give way to (Combat Bible §24).

avoidanceWeight.description: How much it gives way, 0 to 1.

waves.description: The Fluxborn waves (Battleground Bible §17, §18): all three lanes spawn together on one schedule; no wave grows stronger over time.

firstWaveSeconds.description: When the first wave spawns, in match-clock seconds (§17: 0:30).

phases.description: Spans of the match with their own cadence, in order, the first from 0. Each wave follows the last by the interval of the phase the last spawned in, so no wave is duplicated or skipped at a boundary (§17).

fromSeconds.description: When the phase begins, in match-clock seconds.

intervalSeconds.description: Seconds from each wave spawned in the phase to the next.

siegeEveryWaves.description: Every this many waves brings siege units; 0 for none.

units.description: Every wave's units, front line first.

siegeUnits.description: Added to the waves that bring siege units, behind the front line.

inhibitorDownUnits.description: Added to each wave of a lane whose enemy inhibitor is down (§18).

unitIntervalSeconds.description: Seconds between one unit of a wave leaving the base and the next, so they walk out in a file.

species.description: Every species, keyed by its stable ID.

ai.description: How every creature's server controller behaves.

thinkSeconds.description: How often it reconsiders its target, in seconds of world time.

corpseSeconds.description: How long a fallen creature's body stays.

homeAcceptance.description: How close to its spot a creature walking home must come to be home.

camps.description: Team A's camps; Team B's are their mirror.

fluxWells.description: The North and South Flux Wells (Battleground Bible §6; ADR-014 §4). What a secure grants is Flux.json's and Economy.json's.

sites.description: Where each Well stands: on the river, so each is its own mirror.

timing.description: Opening and cycle (§6: they open at 6:00, and a secured Well waits 5 minutes).

openSeconds.description: When the Wells first open, in match-clock seconds.

respawnSeconds.description: How long after its secure a Well opens again.

radius.description: How near its centre a Vanguard must stand to count as present.

presence.description: How allied Vanguards standing at an open Well drain it (§6).

tickSeconds.description: How often presence drains it, in seconds of world time.

drainPerSecond.description: Health drained per second by one Vanguard alone.

drainPerAdditional.description: Added per second by each further Vanguard counted.

maxCounted.description: The most Vanguards of one side that count (§6: a dogpile is not required).

contestedFactor.description: Contested, the side with more drains at this fraction of the rate for its lead; equal sides stall it.

regeneration.description: An open Well nobody works on heals.

idleSeconds.description: How long without damage or presence before it heals.

fractionPerSecond.description: Health restored per second, as a fraction of its Max Health.

replication.description: How often the battleground's units replicate, as whole fractions of the server's tick (ADR-011 §7; amends ADR-006 §5).

fluxbornUpdateEveryServerTicks.description: A Fluxborn sends its state every this many server ticks.
